timecoded_text_to_speech.text: So I'm here with Ann Marie Thompson. She is the Director of Research Partnerships
with NSER and I'll start with saying thank you first off because NSER is the
major funder of seven of our eight networks that fall under fiber. The
smorning we announced that NSERC is is awarding us another year of funding
for knowledge mobilization efforts. Did you elaborate a bit on what is
knowledge mobilization and some of the projects that you're funding for us?
Sure. So my understanding is with this new funding that it will enable
fiber to perhaps host more regional meetings where there'll be a greater
opportunity for the networks to connect at a regional level and to really
get that connection going for stimulating discussions. Also I'm aware that
there's going to be more opportunities for students perhaps to go work in
another network for a while and bring that knowledge back to their own network.
So really promoting more linkages with this funding.
Right and one of the programs that was part of the package is we're going to be
sending a group of students over to Sweden to the Marcus Wallenberg Prize in
in September and this morning we were told that an actual Canadian professor
Dr. Derek Gray from McGill University was awarded that prestigious honor. So the
timing is great. What are your comments on a Canadian researcher winning that?
Well of course I'm very proud as a Canadian and my understanding is that this is
the equivalent of the Nobel Prize in forestry and so just extremely proud that
that is going to a Canadian. Dr. Gray has of course been funded by
INSERC for a long long time and we were able to honor him recently with our
Synergy for Innovation Awards where we're recognizing the best examples of
long standing contributions between an academic and an industrial partner.
So Dr. Gray's work is fabulous and very proud. Well thank you so much and
thanks to INSERC for supporting all of the innovative forestry work going on.
Great thank you.
